result.final_text:
## What this letter says
You were in hospital from 5 October 2026 to 7 October 2026.
You had a chest infection (community-acquired pneumonia). It was in the lower part of your right lung.
Your CURB-65 score was 1. This is a score doctors use to judge how serious a chest infection is.
In hospital, you had antibiotics into a vein (IV) for 1 day. Then you had amoxicillin tablets.
You may feel tired for several weeks.
Your cough may last 3 to 6 weeks.

## What you need to do
1. Take your amoxicillin tablets for 3 more days. This makes 5 days of antibiotics in total.
2. Have a repeat chest X-ray in 6 weeks at the Radiology Department. It checks that the infection has cleared.
3. You do not need to book the chest X-ray. A request has been sent.

## Dates and medicines
- 5 October 2026: you were admitted to hospital.
- 7 October 2026: you left hospital.
- 10 October 2026: your last dose of amoxicillin.
- In 6 weeks: repeat chest X-ray at the Radiology Department. The exact date is not given.

Medicine:
- Amoxicillin, 500 milligrams, three times a day (TDS).
- You have had 2 days of antibiotics in hospital.
- You take tablets for 3 more days.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- When will I get the date for my chest X-ray?
- How will I hear about my chest X-ray?
- What can I do if I still feel tired after several weeks?

## When to get urgent help
See your GP or call 111 if:
- you become more short of breath
- your fever comes back
- you cough up blood

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*
